> 治人事天，莫若嗇.

Chapter 58 put the ruler down. Chapter 59 gives one action, and it is agricultural.

## 嗇 is bringing the harvest into the granary

嗇 is built on 來 and 回. 來 is wheat. 回 is to circle — going around the granary to bring it in.

So 嗇 is not "stinginess." It is: the grain has been reaped, and it is being brought home.

The whole chapter follows from this. It is not about spending less; it is about completing the harvest.

## 早服

> 夫唯嗇，是謂早服.

服: to submit, to take up service — and also to set out on a road, to take one's place in a line.

早服 — early submission, early setting out. Because what has been brought in is already in the store, the next season begins from a position of sufficiency rather than from deficit.

## 重積德

重 — layer on layer, the same 重 as in 重積. Accumulation that has thickness.

And the chain that follows is a ladder:

> 早服謂之重積德；重積德則無不克；無不克則莫知其極；莫知其極，可以有國；有國之母，可以長久.

Nothing not overcome; then no known limit; then a state can be held; then the mother of the state, and long endurance.

## 克 is a shoulder

克: 肩也 — the shoulder, and by extension to carry, to bear up under.

無不克 is therefore not "conquers everything." It is: there is nothing it cannot carry. The accumulation has made the shoulders able to bear the load.

Which changes the whole ladder. What is being described is capacity — the ability to hold more without collapsing — and capacity is what a granary is.

## 深根固柢

Deep roots, firm base. 柢 is the main root, the one that goes straight down.

深根固柢，長生久視之道 — the way of long life and long seeing.

久視 is the striking phrase: long seeing. Not merely living long — remaining able to see for a long time.

And 視 is the same character as chapter 1's 視之不見 and chapter 14's 視. The one whose root is deep keeps his sight.

## Why 嗇 and not 儉

The two words are close and the chapter chooses the agricultural one.

儉 is a limit on consumption. 嗇 is the act of bringing in. One is a restriction; the other is a completion.

A person who practices 儉 manages what he has. A person who practices 嗇 finishes the cycle — and a finished cycle is what makes the next one possible without strain.

## The chain of the three chapters

57: add no affairs.
58: because the ground moves, no fixed standard holds.
59: so the one thing to do is bring the harvest in — build the store, and everything downstream follows.

It is the most practical sequence in the book: not a policy, not a standard, but a stock.

## A test

Take the work you did this year that produced something durable — a method, a relationship, a piece of writing, a saved amount. Then ask whether you brought it in, or whether it is still standing in the field, exposed.
